ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act); Companies Act 1993; Companies (Register of Ultimate Holding Company and Significant Control) Amendment Act 2023; Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT codes and guidelines; Companies Office AML/CFT requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization required for domestic origin; if used offshore in an Apostille Convention state, obtain a New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Apostille; if used in a non-Apostille state, complete MFAT authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination country's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. Never chain Apostille and Consular Legalization.

If required offshore in an Apostille state, MFAT Apostille; in a non-Apostille state, MFAT authentication plus Consular Legalization at the relevant foreign consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation and banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand company directors/shareholders or a notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution or power of attorney in its country of execution; if the executing country is an Apostille Convention state, affix an Apostille; if not, complete consular legalization at the New Zealand embassy or consulate in that country. Apostille route is not used for non-member states and consular legalization is not added to an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand company shareholders or the New Zealand Companies Office if a default constitution is adopted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy by a New Zealand notary public; for offshore use in an Apostille state, MFAT Apostille; for use in a non-Apostille state, MFAT authentication plus consular legalization at the destination's consulate in New Zealand. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The company's intended or existing New Zealand or foreign banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead and notarized by a notary public; if the bank is in an Apostille Convention state, Apostille issued by the competent authority of that state; if the bank is in a non-member state, consular legalization by the destination jurisdiction's consulate in the bank's country. No document may receive both an Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, UBO, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner against New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) watchlists, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the consolidated EU sanctions list, supplemented by continuous adverse-media and politically exposed person (PEP) checks using a commercial risk-scoring database. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate, including independent verification of source of wealth and funds before approval. All screening results are documented in an auditable compliance file with date-and-time stamps and retained for at least five years under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 1996, as applicable. The low-risk standard tier does not eliminate these obligations; it only affects ongoing customer due diligence frequency and simplified measures where legally permitted by the Department of Internal Affairs supervision regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols_ex: The domestic supervisor may be the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) or Financial Markets Authority (FMA) depending on the reporting entity; the company itself is not a reporting entity unless it becomes a financial service provider, but the formation agent, law firm, and bank are subject to sectoral AML/CFT obligations and must independently perform the screening above and rely on the UBO declaration, obtaining evidence of identity and beneficial ownership before incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Business Name Check and online incorporation system (available through the Companies Register at registers.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be available in English or te reo Maori, using letters of the English alphabet, numerals, and certain punctuation; they must not be identical or almost identical to an existing name reserved or registered in the New Zealand Companies Register. Where a non-English script is used in marketing, the registered legal name must still conform to the Latin-alphabet transliteration approved by the Registrar, and the company name must end with 'Limited' or its approved abbreviation 'Ltd' unless an exemption under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 applies. A four-tier naming convention applies: (1) the exact proposed legal name, (2) an English transliteration if the desired name is in te reo Maori, (3) a phonetic equivalent for trade-mark-like use, and (4) an alternative structural variant with 'NZ' or industry identifiers if the first choice is unavailable. The Companies Office applies the 'almost identical' test considering singular/plural, spelling variations, punctuation, and related-name identifiers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects the proposed name under the Companies Act 1993 or the Companies (Registration of Company Names) Regulations 2014, the applicant may first file a written request for reconsideration through the Companies Office Contact Centre or an online enquiry within 15 working days of the rejection, explaining why the name is not identical or almost identical to an existing name and why no prohibited token applies. If refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 or the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, within 60 days of the final administrative decision, supported by an affidavit and evidence that the proposed name does not mislead or contravene statute. For names containing restricted words such as 'New Zealand' or 'Royal', ministerial consent from the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet must be obtained before resubmission, and a formal application for the Registrar's discretion should also be made in parallel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_validity_window_days_co: The Companies Office online reservation is generally valid for 20 working days, not 30 days. The official fee is NZ$10.70 (incl. GST) for name reservation via the online register or NZ$26.70 via manual application; official registry fees are integrated into the itemized budget.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand at which documents can be served, and it cannot be a PO Box or a virtual office that does not accept physical service; a commercially available virtual office service may be acceptable only if it includes a physical street address in New Zealand and a person authorized to accept service during normal business hours. For a low-risk online retail company using Stripe and PayPal, the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department generally accepts a virtual office address for tax registration and correspondence if the company maintains real physical books and records at that address or at another verified business or director address, but banks and payment processors typically require a physical business premise or a clear explanation of a home-based or virtual operation with management substance. If the company has no employees, the registered office can be the director's residential or solicitor's office address; however, e-commerce acquiring banks and payment gateways such as Stripe and PayPal may place holds or require additional KYC if the address appears to be only a commercial maildrop. The IRD requires a 'care of' or physical address for contact and can treat a non-substantive virtual mailbox as a red flag for GST registration, therefore the virtual office arrangement should be backed by a physical service agreement and a responsible natural person.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspections are unlikely but not zero. New Zealand Companies Office does not routinely conduct on-site visits, but the Registrar may inspect records under the Companies Act 1993 following a compliance complaint. Inland Revenue may conduct an unannounced visit under the Tax Administration Act 1994 if there is GST or income-tax non-compliance suspicion, especially for e-commerce businesses that fail to register or underreport income. The probability of a physical inspection is estimated at 5-10%; the low risk is attributable to the low-risk online retail model and New Zealand's risk-based compliance system. The checklist to mitigate even this risk includes: ensure the registered office is a physical place; personally ensure a copy of the constitution and share register is available; maintain accounting records in English; file annual returns on time; retain board meeting minutes; display the company number and correct legal name on any website or invoices; and never use a maildrop-only address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly sections 10-18 (constitution and incorporation), section 20 (company name), sections 36-47 (share issue and capitalization), sections 151-153 (appointment and residence of directors), sections 184-187 (registered office), and sections 190-191 (exercise of board powers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 does not impose a minimum issued, paid-up, or escrowed share capital for a New Zealand limited liability company. The Company must issue at least one share to at least one shareholder, and shares may be issued at no par value, fully paid or partly paid, in any currency, and for such consideration as the board determines. There is no statutory blocked escrow account requirement. The initial subscribed capital may be nominal, subject to the board's fiduciary duties and the solvency test under the Companies Act 1993. Non-resident ownership is permitted without restriction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF NZ_LTD

RESOLVED by the Board of Directors of NZ_LTD (the Company) on the date below pursuant to section 190 of the Companies Act 1993, New Zealand, and the Company's constitution:

WHEREAS the Company has been duly incorporated by the New Zealand Companies Office and has registered office, shareholders, and directors as recorded in the Companies Register; and WHEREAS the incorporator has validly subscribed for the initial issued share capital set out in the incorporation application and the board wishes to complete the statutory organization of the Company.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Board acknowledges the subscription of 100 ordinary shares of no par value issued to the initial shareholder, and determines that each share is fully paid or credited as fully paid as recorded in the application. The Board directs the Company to enter the allottee in the share register as the sole holder, to issue the share certificates in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, and to record all capital movements in the register of shares.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [full physical New Zealand street address], New Zealand, which shall be the Company's legal address for the service of process, notices, and official communications. The Board directs the Company Secretary to maintain the registered address with the Companies Register and to notify any change within ten working days as required by law.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [name of bank] as the Company's primary banker. The Board approves the opening of an operating account, a settlement account for e-commerce payment rails, and such reserve or foreign currency accounts as needed. The signatories named in the bank authority, comprising at least one director and such other officers as the Board determines, are authorized to open, operate, and close accounts, sign cheques and electronic instructions, draw payment on the Company's behalf, and establish merchant facilities with Stripe and PayPal.

4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. The Board appoints [full name] as Chief Executive Officer, [full name] as Chief Financial Officer, [full name] as Company Compliance Officer, and [full name] as AML/CFT Compliance Officer. Each appointed officer has authority to execute ordinary-course agreements, engage professional advisers, and perform such functions as delegated by the Board, subject to statutory duties.

5. STATUTORY COMPLIANCE INSTRUCTIONS. The Board instructs the officers to register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department, obtain an IRD number and New Zealand Business Number, assess GST registration obligations, maintain the Company's statutory registers, and file annual returns and all other disclosures required by the Companies Act 1993.

This resolution is effective immediately and is binding on the Company and its officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Corporate Structure Design
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register name search portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation agent must access the Companies Register and test the proposed name NZ_LTD and at least two alternative names to ensure that the selected name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved company name. The name must include the suffix Limited or the authorized abbreviation Ltd, and must not contain prohibited words or expressions unless a statutory consent has been obtained. The incorporator must also determine whether to adopt the statutory default constitution under the Companies Act 1993 or a tailored written constitution. The initial share ownership, any non-resident ownership conditions, proposed director residence, and the intended use of Stripe and PayPal as payment rails should all be confirmed in writing before any statutory filing is made.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name with at least two alternative names
Tailored constitution, if adopted, or confirmation of statutory default
Full legal names, dates of birth and residential addresses of proposed directors and shareholders
Proposed shareholding structure and number of shares to be issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search indicates that a chosen name is unavailable, select an alternative name and resubmit. If the Registrar considers a name objectionable or likely to cause confusion, the applicant may file a fresh application with alternative names or request the Registrar's reconsideration with evidence of prior use and distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Director Consents and Governance Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicant, incorporator and formation agent for subsequent lodgement with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator shall prepare the written consent to appointment as director, signed by each proposed director, together with certified identity documents and proof of residential address. Under the Companies Act 1993, every director must consent in writing to act before the application is filed, and the consent must state the director's full legal name, date and place of birth, residential address and contact details. At least one director must meet the New Zealand or Australia ordinary residence requirement. If a tailored constitution is adopted, it must be dated and signed by the initial shareholder. The formation agent should also prepare an internal board-pack containing the proposed share subscription, registered office, bank mandate and officer appointments for completion by the board after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent to Appointment as Director signed by each proposed director
Certified copy of passport or national identity card for each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address, utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months
Signed constitution, if any
AML/CFT beneficial ownership information of the initial shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries a consent or identity document, the formation agent must replace the defective document with a corrected consent or a certified translation, and resubmit with verified identification. Supplemental evidence of residential address or a statutory declaration may also be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal, using a verified RealMe login
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Companies Register portal with the validated RealMe credential and begin a new company incorporation application. Enter the approved company name, the registered office physical address which must be a real street address in New Zealand, the full names and residential addresses of directors and shareholders, and the exact number and class of shares to be issued. Confirm that the company is not a restricted entity and that no consent of a professional regulator is required for the retail of consumer electronics. Submit the electronic form and pay the statutory filing fee. Upon successful vetting, the Registrar will issue the certificate of incorporation, the New Zealand Business Number, and the Companies Register number, making the entity lawfully able to commence transactions.
required_dossiers: Online incorporation application data
Director and shareholder personal information
Registered office physical address
Payment of the Companies Office filing fee
Consents to appointment and previous governance documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, the applicant must respond to the Companies Office through the online portal within the statutory period, complete or correct the requested details, and resubmit. If the Registrar refuses registration, the applicant may either correct the defect and file afresh, or exercise the review and correction powers available under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand, through myIR and the Business Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the newly issued New Zealand Business Number and certificate of incorporation, register the company with the Inland Revenue Department. Apply for an IRD number and confirm the standard income tax obligations of the company. Register for Goods and Services Tax if the company's taxable supplies in the previous or following twelve-month period are expected to exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily if input credit recovery is advantageous. If the company intends to employ staff, register for PAYE and employer-related levies. The company should also confirm its financial year-end and nominate tax contact details. For an online consumer electronics retail business, identify whether GST applies to domestic sales, export sales, or digital services, and confirm responsibility for collecting GST on sales settled through Stripe and PayPal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
New Zealand Business Number
Director and shareholder tax residence details
Bank account details
Expected turnover and GST registration election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department queries the registration or the GST effective date, correct the information through myIR and provide supporting transaction evidence. If assessments or penalties are imposed, apply to the Commissioner for remission under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and file any overdue returns immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Merchant Payment Rail Setup and Post-Incorporation Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in New Zealand and the New Zealand Companies Office annual return system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, board resolution, director and shareholder identification, and the bank mandate to the chosen New Zealand commercial bank to open the company operating and settlement accounts. Complete the bank's AML/CFT customer due diligence process by disclosing the beneficial owner of the company and the expected transaction profile for online consumer electronics sales. After account activation, connect the company bank accounts to Stripe and PayPal by submitting the incorporation documents, bank account verification, website information, and expected sales channel evidence. The board must then hold the first formal board meeting, ratify the share allotment, approve the final bank signatories, adopt the corporate records, open the statutory registers, and ensure the annual return filing obligation is calendared in the Companies Register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Constitution
First board resolution and bank mandate
Passport and proof of address for directors and beneficial owner
Certified copy of the Companies Register extract
Stripe and PayPal account verification packages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or suspends the application under AML/CFT rules, provide enhanced due diligence documents, clarify the source of funds and expected transaction volume, and submit a revised board resolution. If the Companies Office triggers a late annual return or record entry issue, file the correction or annual return online and pay any penalty, then apply for administrative relief where circumstances justify it.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity carries out no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations under ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx. No industrial licensing board authorizes online consumer electronics retailing in New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as an industrial or manufacturing permit. The Company remains subject to consumer protection and product safety regulations, including the Fair Trading Act 1986, the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993, the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010 for electrical products, and the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 for electronic marketing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - future facility activities would be regulated by the Environmental Protection Authority, the Ministry for the Environment, and the relevant territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the e-commerce retail activity does not cross a statutory threshold requiring a full EIA report or environmental registration. No discharge consent, land use consent, or air discharge permit is required for the current online retail scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the Company has no point-source wastewater discharge, VOC emission stack, or hazardous waste treatment operation. If the Company later receives electronic product returns or handles e-waste, it must comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, the Basel Convention obligations administered by the Environmental Protection Authority, and any relevant territorial authority trade waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at formation for a pure online retail business without physical premises. If the Company later leases an office, fulfilment warehouse, or showroom, it must obtain from the relevant territorial authority a building warrant of fitness or occupancy certificate, fire safety approval coordinated with Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, and register with WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for any workplace operated by the Company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; online electronic portal: Inland Revenue myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: To obtain a New Zealand IRD number (the statutory TIN for income tax and GST purposes), a foreign non-resident entity must first determine whether it is carrying on an activity that creates an NZ tax registration obligation. If the entity will carry on a taxable activity in New Zealand, establish a fixed establishment, supply remote services to NZ consumers, or supply low-value goods (goods at or below NZD 1,000) to NZ consumers, it must obtain an IRD number. The application is made through the prescribed Inland Revenue non-individual IRD number application, either via myIR where access can be enabled, or by paper submission to Inland Revenue, accompanied by certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles or equivalent registry extract, list of directors and ultimate shareholders, confirmation of no bankruptcy/liquidation, and an appointed NZ tax agent or service address if no NZ physical office exists. After IRD number issuance, the same IRD number is used to register for GST; GST registration is applied for online in myIR using the GST registration application. If the foreign entity is actually registered as an overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand, it must first obtain an NZBN through the Companies Office before the tax registration can be finalized. The entity should state the date of commencement of business, projected 12-month supplies, banking details, and whether it is registering as an ordinary NZ GST taxpayer or as an offshore supplier of remote services/low-value goods. Inland Revenue issues the registration confirmation and sets the filing frequency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an NZ-resident limited company is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act 2007 and not a pass-through entity; the company pays 28% corporate income tax on worldwide income and attaches imputation credits to dividends. Non-resident companies are taxed on NZ-source income, and an overseas company with a New Zealand branch is taxed on the branch's NZ-source income at the same corporate rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the US check-the-box sense. New Zealand has no elective corporate pass-through classification for ordinary limited liability companies; a company may elect Look-Through Company status only if it satisfies the statutory LTC eligibility rules, and wholly-owned groups may elect tax consolidation. Hybrid and branch mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 are mandatory and not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) imposed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period, or expected supplies in the next 12 months; non-resident offshore suppliers of remote services and low-value goods (goods consigned to NZ at or below NZD 1,000) are required to register under the offshore supplier registration regime using the same NZD 60,000 threshold; voluntary registration is permitted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not have a real-time electronic invoicing clearance, fiscal pre-authorisation, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime. Inland Revenue does not operate a transactional e-invoice approval API; instead, GST-registered businesses must issue compliant tax invoices within 28 days of a request. E-invoicing through the PEPPOL network is available and is preferred for business-to-government transactions, but there is no universal B2B/B2C digital clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated as an export under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or by the date the Commissioner allows), the supplier does not intend the goods to remain in New Zealand, and the supplier retains evidence of export. For online retail of personal electronics, the zero-rating limb is that the electronics are physically dispatched from New Zealand to an overseas destination; the supply remains a taxable supply, so the exporter can claim input tax credits for related costs and any excess GST credit is refundable. Services supplied by a New Zealand business to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply are zero-rated under section 11A to the extent the services are not connected with New Zealand land or goods and are not performed on the recipient while the recipient is in New Zealand. Supplies of low-value goods by an offshore seller into New Zealand are not export zero-rating events; they are subject to 15% GST at the border or under the offshore supplier rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Export Entry) submitted electronically through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window, quoting the exporter/shipper Customs client code and applicable tariff classification where a formal export declaration is required

Original or authenticated transport document: ocean Bill of Lading, Master/House Air Waybill, or recognized consignment note showing the goods physically departed New Zealand and the overseas destination

Commercial invoice and the GST tax invoice issued by the NZ supplier showing the supply description, value, buyer name/address, and a statement that GST is zero-rated as an export under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
Packing list and proof of ownership/risk transfer using Incoterms, evidencing the sale to a non-resident buyer and transfer of title outside New Zealand

Inward payment and foreign exchange record: bank inward remittance advice, SWIFT MT103, foreign exchange contract, or deposit evidence confirming actual repatriation of sale proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The burden of proving physical export and foreign payment is on the exporter. If the goods are not exported within 28 days (or an extension is not obtained), the zero-rating is void and GST at 15% plus use-of-money interest is assessed from the original time of supply; input tax credits associated with the failed export are clawed back. Inland Revenue may impose shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or similar action. Knowingly false export documents can result in criminal prosecution. Although New Zealand has no statutory 180-day exchange-control repatriation deadline, failure to receive sale consideration within a reasonable period (here benchmarked at 180 days) will heighten audit scrutiny and may lead to transfer pricing adjustments under Part 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007, or to GST denial if the transaction is found to lack commercial substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ); no separate foreign exchange control administration is constituted under New Zealand law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates an open capital and current account under a freely floating exchange-rate regime. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand supervises the financial system but does not impose exchange controls, approval gates, or surrender requirements on New Zealand resident companies. The New Zealand dollar is fully convertible, and trade-related inflows and outflows generally pass without central bank screening. For an online consumer-electronics retailer, inbound equity injections, intercompany loans, platform settlements from Stripe/PayPal, and trade disbursements can be settled in NZD, USD, CNY, EUR, or AUD. There is no requirement to convert export receipts into NZD. Profit remittance is not subject to foreign-exchange permission; however, it is subject to tax compliance gates: New Zealand non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest, possible approved issuer levy if a shareholder loan is subject to interest withholding, and transfer-pricing/loan-structure rules. Because the currency floats, the treasury should operate an active FX risk policy for USD/CNY supplier obligations and delayed platform settlements. Capital account transactions are unrestricted unless the overseas investment triggers the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for sensitive land or significant business assets; the likely retail scope does not, but legal counsel should confirm before large equity transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable in New Zealand. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign-currency receipts. A company may keep export proceeds in an approved foreign-currency account, convert at freely determined bank rates, and use those funds for supplier payments or treasury operations without RBNZ approval. The only reporting duty arises from Inland Revenue for taxation and from the Companies Office for financial reporting, not from foreign-exchange administration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD with foreign-currency sub-accounts)
Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD with foreign-currency sub-accounts)
Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD with foreign-currency sub-accounts)
Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD with foreign-currency sub-accounts)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: New Zealand does not have an EU-style e-money institution licence; non-bank payment providers register as financial service providers under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008 and must comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Providers such as Wise or Airwallex can operate in New Zealand as payment or remittance service providers while holding funds in trust or safeguarding accounts with a licensed bank. They are not banks, cannot provide lending, trade finance, commercial credit facilities, or full treasury sweeps, and their licences do not waive the requirement for a registered bank clearing path. For a low-risk consumer-electronics exporter, an EMI is viable as an auxiliary collection rail for platform payouts and small working-capital transfers, but the primary treasury function should remain a Tier-1 domestic bank account. Legal constraints include FMC Act disclosure requirements, AML/CFT registration with the Department of Internal Affairs, and reliance on licensed NZ banks for ultimate NZD settlement, giving an overall viability rating of Medium for specialised flows and Low for primary banking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate in the Companies Act 1993 requiring directors to appear physically in a bank branch, nor is consular proxy opening broadly recognised by New Zealand banks. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, identity verification must be completed by reliable and independent sources, which permits remote onboarding using electronically verified passports, apostilled corporate extracts, and video interviews if the bank risk appetite accepts them. In practice, Tier-1 banks will often accept a New Zealand-registered director or a solicitor or authorised signatory as the physical contact point, while overseas directors submit certified identity and source-of-funds documentation. For first account opening, most banks require at least one senior officer or director to attend a physical or live video interview; after onboarding, remote signatory authority is normally available. A purely notarised proxy opening without any bank interaction is not generally available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident 100% shareholding with no visible nexus to New Zealand, especially when a BVI or HK holding structure is used and the ultimate beneficial owner is otherwise difficult to identify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the New Zealand Companies Office extract showing NZBN and directors, Register of Members and allotment history, completed UBO declaration for every natural person owning 25% or more, valid passport and proof of residential address, corporate structure chart from ultimate individuals through each intermediary, source-of-wealth statement backed by three years of bank statements or sale and employment contracts, and an independent legal opinion confirming no nominee or concealment arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained volatility in e-commerce settlements, such as high volumes of Stripe or PayPal deposits without matching order-level records, repetitive same-day refunds, or transactions involving sanctioned or high-risk shipping addresses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant portal export with order ID, SKU, product description, shipping address, payment timestamp, and refund or chargeback disposition; monthly platform payout reconciliation statements; PCI DSS attestation or certificate for the e-commerce environment; carrier tracking evidence from NZ Post, FedEx, DHL, or courier partners; documented refund and returns policy; and explanations for any chargeback ratio above the processor threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to electronics wholesalers in grey-market hubs, round-tripping between related parties, or missing customs and import documentation for consumer-electronics inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and proforma invoices from OEMs or authorised distributors, import and export customs declarations filed with the New Zealand Customs Service, bills of lading and air waybills, commercial invoices for each shipment, freight-forwarder statements, transfer-pricing documentation if the supplier is a related party, sanction and PEP screening results for counterparties, and a written attestation that the company does not source counterfeit or non-authorised serial-number inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection, whether as equity or shareholder loan, from an offshore shareholder without clear source of funds or structured through a third-party paying intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the share issue or shareholder loan, updated share register filed at the Companies Office, a signed loan agreement with interest rate and repayment schedule, audited financial statements of the shareholder, shareholder personal tax clearance or dividend vouchers, original SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details showing direct remitter, source-of-funds evidence such as sale of shares or inheritance settlement, and a legal opinion that the Overseas Investment Act threshold is not triggered.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital or shareholder loans should be wired by the shareholder directly to the company Tier-1 NZ bank account using SWIFT MT103, with a transaction narrative such as Share capital contribution - NZ Ltd or Subordinated shareholder loan - NZ Ltd. New Zealand has no exchange-control approval or capital verification certificate requirement; the Companies Office share register and bank deposit notice constitute prima facie evidence of capital contribution. The remitting bank must be an actual financial institution in good standing, not a third-party payer, and the NZ receiving bank will apply sanctions, PEP, and source-of-funds checks on the remitter. If the investment triggers the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for sensitive assets or significant business assets, Overseas Investment Office consent should be obtained before settlement; legal counsel should confirm that ordinary online retail in consumer electronics remains outside screening thresholds. The company should provide its IRD number, registered office, and beneficial-ownership pack to the bank before wiring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments should prioritise SWIFT MT103 for amounts below bank trade-credit limits and for open-account terms. For bulk consumer-electronics purchases from OEMs or distributors, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit at sight, confirmed by a prime New Zealand or offshore bank, protects both buyer and seller where the goods transit is lengthy. Documentary Collections on D/P or D/A terms are permissible only with established counterparties and should be supported by transport documents, commercial invoices, insurance certificates, and pre-shipment inspection reports. Domestic NZD liquidity uses the Reserve Bank Exchange Settlement Account System for clearing; cross-border payments clear via SWIFT, with correspondent banking chains kept to no more than one intermediary bank. All outbound disbursements should be reconciled against the underlying purchase order, customs declaration, and platform inventory plan, with no unrestricted crypto or informal hawala rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNY, and NZD/AUD for trade payables and receivables, generally up to 24 months, supported by underlying purchase orders or platform settlement forecasts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for restricted or non-fully-convertible currencies encountered in procurement, such as CNY/CNH, KRW, INR, or IDR, executed under a New Zealand bank offshore NDF desk and physically cash-settled in NZD
FX swaps for short-term cross-currency liquidity between the NZD operating account and USD or CNY sub-accounts, with no speculative or leveraged extension

Cross-currency interest rate swaps permitted solely to cover defined intercompany debt or long-term supplier credit and subject to transfer-pricing and thin-capitalisation documentation; exotic options, reverse redemptions, and derivative structures without an identified underlying treasury exposure are prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company (Companies Act 1993, Section 208)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the anniversary date of incorporation; for example, an incorporation date of 15 March makes the annual return due no later than 14 April in each subsequent year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approx. USD 60) is imposed after the due date. Continued non-filing may cause the Registrar to issue a Section 318 removal notice, and if no response is provided the company is administratively struck off and dissolved; restoration after strike-off requires a court order or registrar restoration process and may involve additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and Associated Annual Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due by 7 July of the same income year; for a non-standard balance date, the return is due by the 7th day of the seventh month after the end of the accounting period, unless a tax agent extension has been formally granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An initial late filing penalty of NZD 50 applies, rising by a further NZD 250 if the return remains outstanding after three months. Unpaid terminal tax attracts late payment interest at the IRD prescribed rate (currently approximately 10.7% per annum, updated quarterly) on the unpaid amount, and prolonged non-filing may result in default assessments and prosecution of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report Where Statutorily Required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the company; filed with the New Zealand Companies Office for entities that are large or otherwise excluded from the Financial Reporting Act 2013 exemptions, and with the Financial Markets Authority where the company is an FMC reporting entity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and made available to shareholders within five months after the end of each accounting period; the company's accounting period is normally 12 months, making the deadline the last day of the fifth month after balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or audit financial statements is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013, subject to a fine of up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) plus daily penalties for continuing breach; directors may also be exposed to personal liability, disqualification, and restoration orders in serious cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a licensed chartered accountant is required for any New Zealand limited company that is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or that is classified as a large company under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A company is large if, in each of the two most recent consecutive accounting periods, it satisfies at least two of the following three quantitative thresholds: (a) total assets exceed NZD 60,000,000 (approx. USD 36,000,000); (b) total revenue exceeds NZD 30,000,000 (approx. USD 18,000,000); and (c) 80 or more full-time equivalent employees. Audit is also compulsory where shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares requisition an audit, where the company's constitution mandates audit, where a shareholder resolution requires audit, or where another New Zealand statute applicable to the activity (such as certain financial services or regulated sectors) requires certified financial statement audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) under the External Reporting Board (XRB) Accounting Standards Framework, comprising: Tier 1 – full NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards); Tier 2 – NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); Tier 3 – NZ IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities for non-publicly accountable small entities; and Tier 4 – simple format reporting standards for certain smaller entities. All statutory financial reporting is subject to the Companies Act 1993, the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and where applicable the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate 30-day beneficial ownership filing requirement for a standard private limited company; instead, the annual return operates as the statutory annual confirmation of registered shareholding, director, address, and company control details. Share allotments must be delivered to the Companies Office within 10 working days of allotment, and any change of director, registered office, or director residential address must be updated within 20 working days. Any ultimate beneficial owner or person exercising significant control must be accurately reflected in the register of members and in the information confirmed by the annual return. For AML/CFT-regulated activities such as e-commerce payment-rail acceptance, the reporting entity must perform initial and ongoing customer due diligence, identify and verify beneficial owners, maintain updated beneficial ownership records, and apply enhanced monitoring where required, with no annual UBO declaration being filed solely at Companies Office level.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Interest Register of Directors' and Senior Managers' Interests
Minute Book of Director and Shareholder Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 600 per annum for a standard registered office and registered agent arrangement with a New Zealand corporate services provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 45,000 for a compulsory full-scope NZ IFRS audit; USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 for a Tier 3 or Tier 4 SME audit or review engagement where mandated at the lower threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard New Zealand corporate rate of 28% on worldwide income for tax-resident companies; NZ does not impose payroll taxes or capital taxes. Reliefs available to a consumer-electronics e-commerce company include the 15% R&D Tax Credit on eligible R&D expenditure (bright-line approval required), immediate deduction for certain intangible software development costs under s EA 3D, and depreciation on plant and equipment. There are no free-zone or patent-box regimes; however, foreign-source dividends and active business income may be exempt under CFC rules if the entity has sufficient substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; compulsory e-filing through Inland Revenue's myIR portal (IRD eFile system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 is due on the 7th day of the second month after the company's balance date for all straight-year filers (e.g. a 31 March balance date must file by 7 May); tax agents may secure a one-month extension (to 7 June), and late lodgement of tax-return information is subject to automatic penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross sales, interest, dividends and other business income derived from New Zealand sources and, if the company is resident, global income subject to tax. Excludes capital gains unless the business trades property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident NZ Ltd, include only New Zealand-sourced income unless an active trade carried on through a permanent establishment in New Zealand triggers a wider allocation. Attach a tax reconciliation where treaty provisions exempt certain categories; claim foreign-source income of an offshore-registered but NZ-resident company only if not excluded by the CFC attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions/expenses: deductible outgoings under s DA 1, including cost of online goods sold, Stripe/PayPal merchant fees, marketing, freight, website hosting, R&D, salaries and use-of-money interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion deductions to the taxable income nexus. For non-resident vendors selling into New Zealand via online platforms, ensure e-commerce platform and payment-processing costs are properly allocated to the New Zealand retail activity; capital vs revenue boundary and the 'black-hole' or prepayment rules apply to intangibles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss: the accounting-based result before tax losses applied; reconcile net profit under IFRS/GAAP to taxable income after adjusting for non-deductible expenses, non-taxable income, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the NZ company is part of a multinational group, this Box is where transfer pricing errors surface: ensure related-party purchases are at arm's length, including margins for an online distributor of consumer electronics under the TNMM method. If the market is the New Zealand end-customer, the local entity must demonstrate functional performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of tax losses carried forward (if any) that meet the shareholder continuity (49% beneficial ownership) requirement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward requires at least 49% identical ownership and, since 2020, a business continuity test. Non-resident parent must monitor share transfers; any dilution of ownership will extinguish loss pools and mandate a recalculation. Also, if the NZ Ltd is a 'loss-attributing qualifying company' (now mostly repealed) or R&D loss user, special allocations apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net profit minus losses carried forward; if the company has imputation credits, this box feeds the tax computation at 28%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Double-check that NZ-sourced periodical payments (e.g. royalties) subject to final withholding (NRWT) are indicated, and that any amounts already withheld by the payer are claimed as credits to reduce the final tax liability. If the company is a 'non-resident company' making a profit, the income tax is computed at 28% and no dividend withholding tax should be duplicated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable: taxable income at the company rate (28%) less imputation credits, PAYE, RWT credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident shareholder has loaned funds to the NZ Ltd, thin-capitalisation rules (s FE 1) may recharacterise excessive interest as a dividend, increasing the tax payable. The resident withholding credits on interest and dividends are refundable; non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) is separate and is not netted against the company's income tax liability without a DTA application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance and dividend withholding tax record: records dividends paid/resident withholding tax attributed to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a NZ Ltd with non-resident shareholders, a shareholder dividend election (optional 'fully imputed dividend' basis) affects the NRWT rate: imputed dividends can be paid with 0% NRWT under NRWT exemption for fully imputed dividends; otherwise 30% or treaty-reduced. Ensure ICA is maintained and quarterly NRT returns filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For completeness, the IR4 electronic schedule for transfer pricing, country-by-country reporting and related-party disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where NZ Ltd engages in cross-border intercompany sales, financing, licensing, or management charges, it is required to use the OECD's three-tier documentation: Master File, Local File and CbC Report if the group exceeds EUR 750m (approx NZD 1.13 billion) global revenue. The Schedule 17P (related-party disclosures) must list all related-party transactions if those exceed NZD 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4: an initial 'failure to file' penalty of NZD 250 (increasing to NZD 500 if still outstanding after one month) under s 139A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus late-payment interest (UOMI) at the applicable two-monthly rate (currently 8.64% p.a. for taxpayers) and a monthly incremental penalty of 1% on any unpaid tax. Deliberate tax evasion is a criminal offence: a fine of up to NZD 250,000 per offence, imprisonment of up to 5 years, and a shortfall penalty of up to 150% (or 200% for abusive tax positions) of the unpaid tax under s 141.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder, subject to a 15% reduced rate for portfolio interests (less than 10% voting) under most tax treaties and 5% for substantial holdings (≥10% voting); if the dividend is fully imputed and the company elects the fully imputed dividend basis, the New Zealand imputation credit may reduce the NRWT base, in some cases to nil, provided the shareholder is not carrying on a business through a PE in New Zealand.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double-taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must provide the New Zealand payer with (1) a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority; (2) a completed Form IR58 or equivalent 'Certificate of Residence' bearing the foreign tax authority's stamp; (3) a beneficial ownership declaration (Form IR67 in some cases) confirming that the recipient is the sole owner of the income and is not a pass-through/interposition; and (4) if the dividend is fully imputed, an imputation credit memorandum. The payer must lodge an NRWT return (IR67) and retain the documents for 7 years; the Inland Revenue may verify the LOB clause; if the foreign company is a shell, relief will be denied and the full 30% (or 15%) must be withheld plus potential penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by a NZ company to non-resident affiliates is subject to NRWT at 15% (treaty rate often 0% or 10%); royalty payments for use of, or the right to use, intellectual property (trademarks, patents, software) are subject to NRWT at 15%, reduced to 10% or 5% under an applicable DTA, and must be supported by an arm's length licence agreement. New Zealand's thin-capitalisation rules also apply: a non-resident owner's debt-to-equity ratio cannot exceed 60% (or 75% for certain industries); excess interest is recharacterised as a dividend and taxed as such.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: There is no general statutory financial threshold for preparing a Local File; however, the New Zealand Inland Revenue requires contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for any cross-border related-party transaction with significant profit attribution (usually where the aggregate arm's length revenue exceeds NZD 10 million), and the OECD Master File / Local File / CbCR must be filed where the consolidated multinational group revenue is at least EUR 750 million (approximately NZD 1.13 billion), with the Local File covering intercompany transactions above NZD 1 million as reported on Schedule 17P.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the same manner as Caribbean or UAE jurisdictions, but it applies the common-law 'substance over form' doctrine, the general anti-avoidance provision in s BG 1 and s GA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, and the permanent establishment (PE) threshold of Article 5 of the OECD Model Tax Convention. For a consumer-electronics online retail operation, the 'core income-generating activities' of sourcing, warehousing, marketing, and take-or-pay risk assumption in New Zealand are decisive for allocation of profit; an entity with no people, premises, or functions cannot legitimately book the retail margin or claim DTA benefits, and Inland Revenue will treat a sham arrangement as null and reallocate income accordingly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Revenue Evasion and Falsified Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating online sales revenue from the consumer-electronics website (e.g. by failing to report Stripe/PayPal settlement transfers, keeping dual books, or overstating refunds), or transferring profit to a tax-haven affiliate by paying invented management or royalty fees without service provision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 141 and 143 of the Tax Administration Act 1994: shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax (200% for abusive decisions), a criminal fine of up to NZD 250,000 per count, and imprisonment of up to 5 years under s 144. In addition, Inland Revenue can recover unpaid tax plus interim interest and use-of-money penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s 255 of the Companies Act 1993, every director is jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts if the company disposed of assets to egregiously avoid the payment of tax; directors who personally sign or procure a false IR4 may be prosecuted, leading to personal disgorgement of the tax plus interest, a travel ban (outbound bail condition) under the Tax Administration Act, and imprisonment as a secondary liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing artificial cross-border intercompany agreements under which the NZ online retail entity is stripped of all profit (e.g. paying a 40% commission to a Hong Kong or Cayman 'management hub' that performs no operational activity while no transfer-pricing documentation is prepared or provided to the IRD on request).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 13 allows the Commissioner to adjust the income to an arm's length amount; the deficiency may attract a 50% shortfall penalty (or 150% for evasion), and failure to produce contemporaneous TP documentation may trigger a 20% penalty on the undervalued income; where the arrangement is also a 'profit restatement' arrangement under s FE 32, interest recharacterisation applies. Criminal liability arises if false declarations were made in the Schedule 17P or CbCR certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer-pricing disclosures may be prosecuted for criminal tax evasion, exposing them to personal liability for civil restitution of the tax shortfall up to 200%, disqualification as a director under s 383 of the Companies Act 1993, and imprisonment of up to 5 years. The court may also issue a personal asset freezing order or travel ban while proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Compliance with Beneficial Ownership and AML/CFT Registration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the NZ company as a shell that conceals the true non-resident owner (e.g. holding shares via nominee directors), while failing to notify the Companies Office of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or failing to open an AML/CFT compliance programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 when the entity is an 'electronic cash transaction' provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Companies Act 1993 (Part 21, s 220 amended in 2020) fines up to NZD 50,000 for failure to keep a UBO register; under the AML/CFT Act, the company is liable for civil penalties up to NZD 2.5 million and directors/officers up to NZD 1 million for non-compliance; wilful contravention can lead to imprisonment of up to 2 years. If the shell is used for tax evasion, the Income Tax Act penalties above are cumulative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director of a shell company can be personally liable for the entire group's unpaid New Zealand tax under the Companies Act's 'reckless trading' provisions, face a travel ban issued by the High Court, and be individually prosecuted under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2009 with a maximum sentence of 5 years' imprisonment for money laundering; the court may order the forfeiture of personal assets as well as the corporate veil-piercing recovery from the director's estate.
